page: Microsoft Azure E32ds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization and powered by the x86_64 Intel Xeon 8573C processor. The instance provides 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 16 physical cores with multithreading, capable of clock speeds up to 4.2 GHz. The CPU subsystem is configured with a 260 MB Level 3 cache, 2 MB Level 2 cache per core, and hardware support for Intel AMX (tile and int8) and AVX-512 vector instruction sets.

Memory provisioning is configured at 256 GB, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio suited for memory-intensive operations. In addition to remote storage compatibility, the instance bundles 1,888 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, providing fast local ephemeral storage for temporary files, swap space, or high-throughput scratch disks. The instance operates without discrete GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results highlight robust throughput in memory-heavy and multi-threaded evaluations. The system achieves 208.86 GB/s in uncached large-block memory read bandwidth and 90.98 GB/s in uncached write bandwidth. Computational performance demonstrates top-quartile execution in Geekbench single-core (2061.0) and multi-core (17016.0) metrics, along with 54.13 GB/s throughput in static web serving. Furthermore, CPU-driven inference tests show high efficiency on small language models, achieving 373.84 tokens per second in generation tasks, supported by matrix acceleration instructions.

While baseline single-core and database transaction tests like PassMark database operations and Redis SET benchmarks land in middle-tier distributions, the instance prioritizes memory capacity and local I/O bandwidth over raw per-core CPU frequency. This resource balance establishes strong qualitative cost efficiency for architectures where memory footprint dominates compute demands. Azure E32ds_v6 is appropriately matched for in-memory databases, large-scale Redis or Memcached clusters, data transformation pipelines, and memory-intensive enterprise analytics.
description: Microsoft Azure E32ds_v6 is a memory-optimized instance powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processors operating at up to 4.2 GHz across 32 vCPUs (16 physical cores) and Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is equipped with 256 GB of memory, delivering a dense 8 GB per core, and includes 1,888 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage without integrated GPUs. Architectural features include 260 MB of L3 cache alongside AVX-512 and AMX extensions. Benchmark tests reveal strong large-block uncached memory throughput, reaching 208.86 GB/s read and 90.98 GB/s write bandwidth, alongside high multi-core Geekbench ratings and static web throughput of 54.13 GB/s. CPU-based small LLM inference also registers high text generation speeds. The trade-off lies in standard single-core compute performance versus high memory and I/O density. The configuration is particularly effective for in-memory relational and NoSQL databases, memory-bound caching systems, enterprise analytics, and data pipeline processing requiring substantial volatile space and rapid temporary storage.
